To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ILP Bayesian learning approach is a powerful method for generating grammars for biological sequence data, that the grammar generated by our approach has a high predictive accuracy for the biological domain and that the grammar-derived features are the best group of features for NPP prediction.

(a) a NPP grammar can be generated using the ILP Bayesian learning approach; (b) the NPP grammar-derived features improve NPP recognition performance, as measured by the new cost function, RA; (c) the NPP recognition performance measured by the new RA is significantly better than the performance measured by predictive accuracy.

the ILP Bayesian learning from positive examples approach is useful in the biological domain, that the grammar learnt by this method is useful for learning NPP recognition models and that the NPP recognition models learnt by this method are useful for finding novel NPPs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of a Chomsky-like representation of a biological class of proteins to generate a grammar which is used to generate features.

the following questions: (i) can a grammar be learned for a class of biological sequence families; (ii) is the grammar useful for learning a predictor of members of this family; and (iii) is it useful for learning cost effective, comprehensible, predictors of members of this class?
whether Chomsky-style grammars are useful for learning predictors of members of a family of biological sequence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the grammar is useful for learning cost-efficient predictors of NPPs.
the grammar is useful in the sense of being a cost-effective predictor of novel NPPs.
a grammar-based feature set is a good basis for a NPP recognition model, and the best model is one which includes the grammar-derived features.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of grammar representations is a useful strategy in this biological domain.
a NPP grammar has been successfully generated using an ILP approach to learning and that the features derived from this grammar have been shown to be of use in the prediction of new NPPs.
the grammar-derived features have a high RA and that the RA is higher than the RA of models without these features.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the grammar-derived features are useful for NPP recognition.
grammar representations can be useful for learning from positive examples in the biological domain.
grammar representations are useful in the context of learning from biological sequence data.
